extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies preparing CAA section 111(d) state plans, regulated electric generating units (EGUs), and stakeholders (industry, NGOs, RTO/ISOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for states on when and how to include compliance flexibilities (emission trading, averaging, unit-specific mass-based compliance) in CAA section 111(d) state plans for affected EGUs, and the documentation and limitations required to demonstrate equivalent stringency with unit-specific standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHGRP reporting for CCS
rubrics_metrics.description: Any affected unit that employs CCS technology that captures enough CO2 to meet the standard and injects the captured CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR or GHGRP subpart VV; if the emitting EGU sends the captured CO2 offsite, it must transfer the CO2 to a facility subject to the GHGRP requirements, and the facility injecting the CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR or GHGRP subpart VV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These emission guidelines do not change requirements to obtain or comply with a UIC permit. The requirement to transfer captured CO2 to an entity subject to the GHGRP is an element of enforcement of the EGU standard and is intended to avoid duplicative monitoring, reporting, and verification between these guidelines and the GHGRP. The guidelines do not regulate downstream recipients of captured CO2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance metric is tons of CO2 captured by the emitting EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the standard is determined exclusively by the tons of CO2 captured by the emitting EGU; the tons of CO2 sequestered by the geologic sequestration site are not part of that calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA anticipates the quantity sequestered will be substantially similar to captured amounts but enforces compliance based on captured tons at the emitting EGU. Verification that captured CO2 is sent to a geologic sequestration site leverages GHGRP reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of specified compliance flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is finalizing a determination that emission trading, averaging, and unit-specific mass-based compliance are permissible for affected EGUs in certain subcategories and in certain circumstances under these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States are not required to allow these flexibilities; the scope of allowance is tailored to be consistent with preserving the stringency of the EPA's BSER determination and to provide incentives for overperformance. The EPA is finalizing permissibility subject to limitations described in the preamble (e.g., Section X.D.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent stringency requirement (fundamental)
rubrics_metrics.description: States using compliance flexibilities must demonstrate that any such use will achieve a level of emission reduction that is in the aggregate as environmentally protective as each affected EGU individually achieving its rate-based standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement derives from the structure and purpose of CAA section 111: state plans including flexibilities must achieve at least the level of emission reduction that would result if each affected EGU were achieving its presumptive standard of performance (after accounting for any RULOF applications). The EPA will find a state plan 'satisfactory' only if it demonstrates this equivalence for all affected EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and documentation requirements to demonstrate equivalent stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: States must clearly demonstrate how they calculated the aggregate rate-based emission limitation (for rate-based averaging), mass limit (for unit-specific mass-based compliance), or mass budget (for mass-based trading) from unit-specific, rate-based presumptive standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify the specific affected EGUs participating, which flexibility each unit will use, the unit-specific rate-based presumptive standard of performance, and the standard of performance established in the plan for each unit or set of units. The state must document and justify assumptions used in the calculation (e.g., weighting, level of utilization of participating EGUs used to calculate mass limits/budgets). For rate-based trading, the standard coupled with any adjustment for acquisition of compliance instruments is used to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate maintenance of requisite stringency for plan approval
rubrics_metrics.description: States must demonstrate how the compliance flexibility will maintain the requisite stringency—i.e., how the plan will maintain the aggregate level of emission reduction that would be achieved if each unit were individually complying with its rate-based standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state plan must address each affected EGU and show the plan overall achieves at least the level of emission reduction that would result from each affected EGU achieving its presumptive standard. Plans will be reviewed to ensure consistency with CAA section 111's purpose of reducing dangerous air pollution by requiring sources to operate more cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backstop emission rate requirement for mass-based approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: For unit-specific mass-based compliance and mass-based trading, states are required to include a backstop emission limitation (backstop rate) in conjunction with mass-based compliance approaches to ensure equivalent stringency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA requires a backstop rate for both the long-term and medium-term coal-fired subcategories. The backstop helps ensure that a mass limit or budget does not, on its own, permit outcomes inconsistent with the emission reductions that would result from unit-specific rate-based standards. States must also show that utilization assumptions underlying mass calculations are appropriately conservative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on inclusion of RULOF sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission trading or averaging programs must not include affected EGUs for which states have invoked RULOF to apply less stringent standards of performance; affected EGUs with RULOF are also prohibited from using unit-specific mass-based compliance under these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RULOF sources have bespoke standards tailored to unique circumstances and are unlikely to overperform; their participation could allow non-RULOF sources to underperform by obtaining compliance instruments, undermining equivalent stringency. The bespoke nature of RULOF makes it difficult to design mass-based strategies that ensure equivalence given uncertainty about future utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on inclusion of natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission trading or averaging programs may not include affected EGUs in the natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories; affected EGUs in these subcategories are prohibited from using unit-specific mass-based compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subcategories' BSER determinations and degrees of emission limitation do not require improvement in emission performance and already offer flexibility to account for varying efficiency; they are unlikely to respond to incentives to overperform and could undermine program equivalence if included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based mechanisms more straightforward to demonstrate equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based averaging and trading, demonstrating an equivalent level of emission reduction is relatively straightforward because the aggregate rate-based emission limitation or adjusted rate-based standard is calculated based on both emission output and gross generation output (utilization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rate-based compliance flexibility inherently adjusts for changes in utilization and preserves the imperative to operate more cleanly, providing relatively stronger assurance of equivalence compared to mass-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative utilization assumptions required for mass-based mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: States employing mass-based mechanisms must show why the assumptions underlying the calculation of utilization for establishing a mass limit or mass budget are appropriately conservative to ensure equivalent emission reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because mass limits/budgets alone may not guarantee commensurate reductions with cleaner performance, states must justify utilization assumptions and include safeguards (e.g., backstop rates) to prevent erosion of required emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibilities cannot change the underlying standard of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any flexibilities involving aggregate compliance would be used to demonstrate compliance with an already-established standard of performance, rather than used to establish a standard of performance in the first instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compliance flexibility may change how an affected EGU demonstrates compliance (e.g., surrendering allowances), but it does not alter the benchmark of emission performance used to evaluate compliance. States including trading or averaging do not need to undergo RULOF for participating sources because the underlying standards remain the EPA's presumptive standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review and lack of presumptively approvable trading/averaging approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is not providing a presumptively approvable approach to emission trading or averaging and intends to review emission trading or averaging programs in state plans on a case-by-case basis against the foundational principles for consistency with CAA section 111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States proposing trading or averaging must therefore demonstrate equivalence and meet the foundational principles; EPA will evaluate design specifics (e.g., participant identification, calculations, assumptions, safeguards) on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirement for state plans including flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to subpart Ba, states are required to conduct meaningful engagement on all aspects of their state plans with pertinent stakeholders, which necessarily includes any potential use of flexibilities for sources to demonstrate compliance through emissions trading or averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful engagement provides an opportunity for communities most affected to provide input, including on any impacts from the use of compliance flexibilities. States may also add further features to address concerns (e.g., environmental justice) or forgo flexibilities entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for coal subcategories to participate and cross-subcategory trading
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is allowing affected EGUs in the medium- and long-term coal-fired subcategories to utilize compliance flexibilities, and is not finalizing a restriction on trading or averaging across these two coal subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA believes overperformance among these sources is possible and worth incentivizing. States may design programs that allow medium-term and long-term coal-fired EGUs to trade or average compliance, subject to the general requirements for demonstrating equivalent stringency and any applicable safeguards (e.g., backstop rates for mass-based approaches).
